references.text: Matthew's parallel account of the same event where a man comes to Jesus, kneels, and asks him for help with his demon-possessed son.
Mark's parallel account where a father from the crowd comes to Jesus and tells him about his son who is possessed by an evil spirit.
Luke also uses the word 'μονογενής' (only begotten) here regarding the widow's only son in Nain, showing a thematic link to the only son mentioned in Luke 9:38.
Jairus' daughter is also described as 'μονογενής' (only daughter), which thematically connects this event to Luke 9:38 where the father asks for help with his only son.
The word 'μονογενής' (only begotten/only) is used of God's Son, the same rare word that the father uses about his only son in Luke 9:38.
The continuation of the account where Jesus heals the boy, showing that Jesus' response to the father's prayer was to cast out the evil spirit and return the boy to his father.
